findings.blocking_reason: Both code paths return false so SQL expressions are correctly disabled today; the concern is maintainability and pattern consistency, not an active vulnerability or broken behavior.
findings.body:
enableSqlExpressions at pkg/expr/reader.go:194-200 reads the flag then ignores it — both branches return false:
- flag OFF → enabled = !false = true → if enabled { return false } → false
- flag ON → enabled = !true = false → skip if → return false → false

Every other flag in the expr package (FlagMlExpressions, FlagRecoveryThreshold, FlagExpressionParser) uses IsEnabledGlobally to actually gate behavior. This is the only flag read whose value is discarded. The ! negation is a trap: a future maintainer could "fix" the logic by removing the return false statements and unintentionally re-enable the CVE-2024-9264 vulnerable SQL parsing path.
findings.suggestion:
Preferred: Remove the flag entirely — delete from toggles_gen.go, registry.go, toggles_gen.json, frontend types. Replace call site with unconditional error return.
If flag must stay: Replace enableSqlExpressions body with return false + CVE comment, and update the doc comment to Deprecated: permanently disabled due to CVE-2024-9264.
findings.title: FlagSqlExpressions gate violates codebase flag-gating pattern

findings.blocking_reason: Missing regression test is not a build/test break, security vulnerability, data loss, API break, or behavior regression — the defense itself is already implemented in this PR.
findings.body:
The security gate at `reader.go:128-132` is the **primary user-facing defense** for CVE-2024-9264: when `QueryTypeSQL` is the query type, the reader calls `enableSqlExpressions(h)` and, if disabled, returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. This is the only thing preventing a user-supplied SQL expression from being parsed and dispatched to `NewSQLCommand`.

Despite being the linchpin of the fix, **there is no test anywhere in the repository that asserts this behavior**. I verified this by:
1. Reading `reader_test.go` in full — it contains only `TestReaderReduceMode`, which exercises the `QueryTypeReduce` case. There is no `TestReaderSQL`, no `TestReadQuery_SQLDisabled`, nothing touching the `QueryTypeSQL` switch case.
2. Grepping the entire `pkg/expr` tree for `sqlExpressions is not implemented` — the only hit is the source line itself in `reader.go:131`. No test references this error string.
3. Grepping for `QueryTypeSQL|enableSqlExpressions|sqlExpressions` across `pkg/expr` — the only test-file hit is `query_test.go:84`, which merely registers `QueryTypeSQL` as a discriminator for schema building, not a behavior test.

**Why this matters for security:** The PR narrative explicitly flags the risk: *"The `enableSqlExpressions` function has misleading dead code... a future developer could 'fix' this and re-enable the vulnerability."* Without a regression test asserting that a `QueryTypeSQL` query produces the disabled-error, a future commit that flips `enableSqlExpressions` to `true` (or removes the `if !enabled` guard) would pass CI silently. The security posture is enforced only by code review, not by the test suite. A regression test is the durable mechanism that survives code churn.

The test should construct an `ExpressionQueryReader` (e.g. `NewExpressionQueryReader(featuremgmt.WithFeatures())` — the same pattern used in `TestReaderReduceMode`), feed it a query with `"type": "sql"`, and assert that `ReadQuery` returns an error containing `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"`.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `reader_test.go` (162 lines total) contains only `TestReaderReduceMode` — confirmed by reading the full file. It constructs `NewExpressionQueryReader(featuremgmt.WithFeatures())` at line 142 and calls `reader.ReadQuery` at line 144, but the test data's `"type"` is always `"reduce"` (lines 36, 57, 80, 102, 123). No test case uses `"type": "sql"`.
Step 2: `grep -r 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' pkg/expr/` returns exactly one match: `reader.go:131` (the source). No test file references this error string.
Step 3: `grep -r 'QueryTypeSQL|enableSqlExpressions' pkg/expr/ --include='*_test.go'` returns only `query_test.go:84` (`Discriminators: data.NewDiscriminators("type", QueryTypeSQL)`) — a schema-registration line, not a behavior assertion.
Step 4: Therefore the code path `reader.go:128-132` (case `QueryTypeSQL` → `enableSqlExpressions(h)` returns false → `return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`) has zero test coverage. A mutation that changes `if !enabled` to `if enabled`, or that makes `enableSqlExpressions` return `true`, would not be caught by any test.
findings.suggestion:
Add a test to `pkg/expr/reader_test.go` mirroring the `TestReaderReduceMode` structure, but for the `QueryTypeSQL` case:

```go
func TestReaderSQLDisabled(t *testing.T) {
	bytes := []byte(`{
		"refId": "B",
		"datasource": {"type": "__expr__", "uid": "__expr__"},
		"expression": "SELECT * FROM A",
		"type": "sql"
	}`)
	var q data.DataQuery
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(bytes, &q))
	raw, err := json.Marshal(q)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	iter, err := jsoniter.ParseBytes(jsoniter.ConfigDefault, raw)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	reader := NewExpressionQueryReader(featuremgmt.WithFeatures())
	_, err = reader.ReadQuery(q, iter)
	require.Error(t, err)
	require.Contains(t, err.Error(), "sqlExpressions is not implemented")
}
```

This locks in the disabled posture and fails loudly if anyone re-enables the path.
findings.title: No regression test asserts QueryTypeSQL returns the 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error

findings.blocking_reason: This is a pre-existing UX/consistency issue about misleading schema advertisement versus unconditional rejection — not a build break, security vulnerability, data loss, API contract break, or regression introduced by this PR.
findings.body: The change at `query_test.go:83-94` perpetuates this inconsistency by keeping the SQL type registered in the schema builder without addressing the backend's unconditional rejection or fixing the misleading feature flag description. The schema description "requires the sqlExpression feature flag" is actively misleading. It implies users can enable SQL expressions by turning on the `sqlExpressions` feature flag. But `enableSqlExpressions` returns false unconditionally — the feature flag is never actually checked in a way that could enable the feature. Both branches of the conditional return false. This means: The advertisement is not removed (SQL still in `query.types.json` with examples and saveModel). The rejection error `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"` is not clear enough — it suggests a temporary implementation gap rather than a permanently disabled feature, and contradicts the schema's claim about feature flag gating. Users who follow the schema's guidance will hit an unconditional rejection regardless of their feature flag configuration.
findings.evidence:
The changed location (`pkg/expr/query_test.go:83-94`) registers the SQL query type in the schema builder with discriminator `type=sql` and example `SELECT * FROM A limit 1`. This registration feeds the schema served to frontend/API clients.

Three relying locations break consistency with the change:

1. Schema served to frontend (`pkg/expr/query.types.json`, embedded at `query.go:110`, exposed via `QueryTypeDefinitionListJSON()` at `query.go:112`, registered as API in `pkg/registry/apis/query/register.go:62`): Still contains the full SQL query type entry with:
   - `name: "sql"`, discriminator `type=sql`
   - Description: "SQLQuery requires the sqlExpression feature flag"
   - Example: "SELECT * FROM A LIMIT 1"
   - This actively guides API clients and frontend users to try SQL expressions.

2. Backend rejection (`pkg/expr/reader.go:128-132`): Rejects SQL with error `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"`.

3. `enableSqlExpressions` function (`pkg/expr/reader.go:194-199`): Always returns false — both branches of the conditional return false, regardless of the feature flag state:
   ```go
   func enableSqlExpressions(h *ExpressionQueryReader) bool {
       enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)
       if enabled {
           return false
       }
       return false
   }
   ```
findings.title: SQL expression advertisement in Grafana's expression query API schema must not guide users into a broken flow — either remove the advertisement or make the rejection error clear enough that users understand the feature is disabled.

findings.blocking_reason: Confirmed regression of HTTP status code from 400 to 500 for the same client request path, which changes behavior clients and monitoring depend on.
findings.body:
The new SQL expressions feature gate at `reader.go:131` returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` — a bare error without `errutil` typing. The HTTP error handler `response.ErrOrFallback` uses `errors.As(err, &grafanaErr)` to select the status code; a bare error fails this assertion and falls back to HTTP 500. Pre-PR, the same request reached `NewSQLCommand` which returned `errutil.BadRequest(...)`, producing HTTP 400.

Key conclusions:
1. HTTP status regression confirmed: 400 → 500. Client error (using disabled feature) misreported as server error.
2. No message leak: The "not implemented" string does NOT appear in the HTTP response body (only "Query data error"). The bare error is server-side log only.
3. Always fires: `enableSqlExpressions` is dead code returning `false` unconditionally, so every SQL expression request hits this path.
4. Fix: Use `errutil.BadRequest("sqlExpressions.disabled", errutil.WithPublicMessage(...))` (400, parity) or `errutil.NotImplemented(...)` (501, semantic). Add errutil import to reader.go.
5. Dead-code control flow and missing tests are being reviewed by other dimensions — not duplicated here.
findings.evidence: POST /ds/query → QueryMetricsV2 → QueryData → TransformData → BuildPipeline → buildGraph → buildCMDNode → ReadQuery → bare fmt.Errorf → handleQueryMetricsError → ErrOrFallback(500) → errors.As fails → Error(500, "Query data error") → HTTP 500.
findings.suggestion: Use `errutil.BadRequest("sqlExpressions.disabled", errutil.WithPublicMessage(...))` (400, parity) or `errutil.NotImplemented(...)` (501, semantic). Add errutil import to reader.go.
findings.title: HTTP status regression confirmed: 400 → 500

findings.blocking_reason: Both paths currently block SQL execution (the legacy path hits the db.go 'not implemented' stub), so there is no live vulnerability; the finding concerns a hypothetical future re-implementation of db.go and missing test coverage, which are non-blocking.
findings.body:
The PR's security boundary — `enableSqlExpressions()` in reader.go:194 — only covers ONE of TWO code paths that create SQL commands. `buildCMDNode` (nodes.go:109) branches on `FlagExpressionParser`:

1. GATED path (nodes.go:123-146): When `FlagExpressionParser` is ON, it calls `reader.ReadQuery`, which hits `enableSqlExpressions(h)` at reader.go:129 — always returns false, blocks SQL.
2. UNGATED path (nodes.go:148-163): When `FlagExpressionParser` is OFF, the switch statement dispatches `case TypeSQL:` (nodes.go:159) directly to `UnmarshalSQLCommand(rn)` with NO `enableSqlExpressions` check.

Per `pkg/services/featuremgmt/toggles_gen.csv:151`, `expressionParser` is `false` by default in production. This means the DEFAULT code path for SQL expression commands is the UNGATED legacy path. The `enableSqlExpressions` gate presented as the CVE-2024-9264 fix is only reached when a non-default feature flag is enabled.

The sole defense on the default path is the stub `db.go` returning `"not implemented"`. If a future developer re-implements `db.go` (re-adds a SQL engine) or "fixes" the misleading dead code in `enableSqlExpressions` (reader.go:195-199 computes `enabled` from the flag but returns false in both branches), the legacy path would have NO security gate whatsoever.

Both contributing findings confirm that ZERO tests verify either path: all 16 parser tests and the sql_command test are `t.Skip()'d`. No test asserts that `enableSqlExpressions` returns false, no test asserts that the legacy `case TypeSQL:` path fails, and no test asserts that the db.go stub blocks execution. The skipped tests make this architectural gap invisible — a regression that re-opens either path would not be caught by CI.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: nodes.go:123 `if toggles.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagExpressionParser)` — gated path goes through reader.ReadQuery.
Step 2: nodes.go:148 `switch commandType {` — legacy path bypasses reader.go entirely.
Step 3: nodes.go:159 `case TypeSQL: node.Command, err = UnmarshalSQLCommand(rn)` — calls UnmarshalSQLCommand directly, no enableSqlExpressions check.
Step 4: toggles_gen.csv:151 `expressionParser,experimental,@grafana/grafana-app-platform-squad,false,true,false` — flag is OFF by default in prod.
Step 5: reader.go:194-199 `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but returns `false` in both the `if enabled` and fall-through branches — dead code that implies gating exists where it doesn't on the legacy path.
Step 6: parser_test.go — all 16 tests begin with `t.Skip()`; sql_command_test.go:9 `t.Skip()` — no test covers either path.
Step 7: graph.go:282 `node, err = buildCMDNode(rn, s.features)` — confirms buildCMDNode is the production entry point.
findings.suggestion: Add a gate check to the legacy `case TypeSQL:` path in nodes.go (mirror the `enableSqlExpressions` check or return an error directly). Un-skip at least one test per path that asserts the 'not implemented' / 'not enabled' failure. Add a test specifically for the legacy path (FlagExpressionParser OFF) to verify SQL commands are rejected. Consider removing the misleading dead code in `enableSqlExpressions` — either make it a clean `return false` with a comment explaining why, or actually implement the gate logic.
findings.title: Security gate only protects the non-default code path — legacy TypeSQL path in nodes.go is ungated and unverified by any test

findings.blocking_reason: The SQL path is currently stubbed with 'not implemented' and the finding describes only a hypothetical future maintenance risk, not a present exploit, regression, or broken build.
findings.body:
The combination of three conditions creates a plausible regression vector for re-enabling the CVE-2024-9264 SQL expressions feature during routine maintenance:

1. UNGATED PATH: The `buildCMDNode` switch block (nodes.go:148-160) calls `UnmarshalSQLCommand(rn)` at line 160 with NO `enableSqlExpressions` gate check. This path is reached when `FlagExpressionParser` is disabled (the `if` at nodes.go:123 falls through to the `switch` at line 148). The ONLY barrier on this path is the db.go stub returning `errors.New("not implemented")`. By contrast, the reader.go:128-138 path IS gated by `enableSqlExpressions` — but the nodes.go switch path bypasses that gate entirely.

2. MISLEADING SKIPPED TESTS: The 16 skipped parser tests (parser_test.go) assert the OLD success behavior (`assert.Nil(t, err)`, `tables[0]` access). If a contributor unskips them during routine test-cleanup, every test fails with "error serializing sql: not implemented". There is NO comment in parser_test.go explaining why the tests are skipped or referencing CVE-2024-9264 — the file looks like ordinary skipped tests, not a security disablement.

3. MISSING GATE TEST: No test anywhere verifies that `enableSqlExpressions` returns false, that the nodes.go TypeSQL path fails, or that the db.go stubs return "not implemented".

Combined escalation chain: unskip tests (routine cleanup) → 16 tests fail asserting SQL SHOULD work → contributor re-implements db.go stubs to make tests pass → nodes.go:159 ungated SQL path becomes active → no gate test catches the regression. The `enableSqlExpressions` gate (reader.go:194-200) only protects the reader.go path, NOT the nodes.go switch path.

Neither finding alone captures this escalation: Finding 1 identifies the missing gate test but not the misleading assertions or the ungated nodes.go path. Finding 2 identifies the misleading assertions but not the ungated path or the missing gate test. The compound is the escalation chain itself — a latent regression vector that activates during routine maintenance, worse than any individual gap.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: nodes.go:123 `if toggles.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagExpressionParser)` — when false, falls through to switch at line 148.
Step 2: nodes.go:159-160 `case TypeSQL: node.Command, err = UnmarshalSQLCommand(rn)` — NO enableSqlExpressions check. Calls UnmarshalSQLCommand → NewSQLCommand → sql.TablesList → db.RunCommands.
Step 3: reader.go:194-200 `enableSqlExpressions` always returns false (both `if enabled { return false }` and fallthrough `return false`) — but this function is ONLY called from reader.go:129, NOT from nodes.go:159.
Step 4: db.go:16-18 `RunCommands` returns `"", errors.New("not implemented")` — the sole barrier on the nodes.go path.
Step 5: parser_test.go lines 10,19,28,40,49,58,67,77,90,103,116,126,133,152,201,210 — all 16 tests have `t.Skip()` with NO comment explaining the security disablement or referencing CVE-2024-9264.
Step 6: parser_test.go lines 13,22,31,43,52,61,70,82,94,108,119,128,143,191,203,212 — all assert `assert.Nil(t, err)` expecting success; many access `tables[0]` expecting non-empty results.
Step 7: sql_command_test.go:9 — TestNewCommand also `t.Skip()`'d, also asserts old success behavior (lines 10-26).
Step 8: grep confirms no test file contains assertions for enableSqlExpressions returning false, nodes.go TypeSQL path failure, or db.go stub errors.
findings.suggestion:
1. Add a gate test asserting `enableSqlExpressions` always returns false (covers reader.go path).
2. Add a test asserting the nodes.go `case TypeSQL` path fails even when `FlagExpressionParser` is disabled — this is the ungated path that currently has zero coverage.
3. Either delete the 16 skipped parser tests or replace them with tests asserting the 'not implemented' failure. Do NOT leave them asserting success behavior — they are a misleading signal.
4. Add a comment at nodes.go:159 explaining this path is intentionally stubbed for CVE-2024-9264 and must not be re-enabled without adding an `enableSqlExpressions` gate check.
5. Consider adding an `enableSqlExpressions` check directly to the nodes.go:159 path rather than relying solely on the db.go stub — defense in depth.
findings.title: Ungated nodes.go SQL path + skipped tests asserting success + missing gate test = latent CVE-2024-9264 re-enablement vector

findings.blocking_reason: The function always returns false, so SQL expressions remain correctly disabled; this is a code clarity/maintainability concern, not a current functional or security regression.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: reader.go:129 `enabled := enableSqlExpressions(h)` is called in `case QueryTypeSQL`.
Step 2: reader.go:194-200 `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (line 195).
Step 3: Line 196 `if enabled { return false }` — when flag is OFF, `enabled` is true, returns false.
Step 4: Line 199 `return false` — when flag is ON, `enabled` is false, also returns false.
Step 5: Both branches return false regardless of `FlagSqlExpressions`. The `enabled` variable is dead. The function is equivalent to `func(...) bool { return false }` but obscures that fact.
findings.title: enableSqlExpressions contains misleading dead-code `enabled` variable that always returns false

findings.blocking_reason: Missing tests for stub methods is a test coverage gap, not a build, security, data, or contract break.
findings.body:
The new `db.go` is a 26-line stub where all three methods (`TablesList`, `RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`) return `errors.New("not implemented")`. This is the **dependency-removal layer** of the CVE-2024-9264 defense: even if the `enableSqlExpressions` gate were bypassed, the SQL engine itself is gone — these methods no longer invoke DuckDB.

**No test asserts that these methods return "not implemented".** I verified:
1. `pkg/expr/sql/` contains only `db.go`, `parser.go`, and `parser_test.go`. There is no `db_test.go`.
2. `parser_test.go` (16 tests) calls `t.Skip()` in **every** test and references the package-level `TablesList` from `parser.go` (not the `(db *DB) TablesList` method). None of them test the `*DB` methods directly.
3. Grepping `pkg/expr/sql/` for `not implemented` returns only the three source lines in `db.go` — no test asserts these error strings.

**Why this matters:** The security fix relies on these stubs remaining stubs. If a future commit re-introduces a real DuckDB-backed implementation (e.g. to "restore a feature"), no test would flag the regression. The stubs are the physical manifestation of the dependency removal; they should be guarded by tests that assert the "not implemented" contract so any re-implementation is a conscious, reviewable decision that updates the tests.

This is `important` rather than `critical` because the `enableSqlExpressions` gate in `reader.go` is the primary gate — `db.go` is defense-in-depth. But defense-in-depth only works if each layer is independently verified.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `db.go:12-22` — three methods, each body is `return ..., errors.New("not implemented")`.
Step 2: `find pkg/expr/sql -name '*_test.go'` → only `parser_test.go`. No `db_test.go` exists.
Step 3: `parser_test.go` — all 16 test functions begin with `t.Skip()` (lines 10, 19, 29, 40, 49, 58, 67, 77, 90, 103, 116, 127, 133, 152, 201, 210). They call the package-level `TablesList` from `parser.go:22`, not the `(db *DB)` methods.
Step 4: `grep -rn 'not implemented' pkg/expr/sql/` → matches only at `db.go:13,17,21`. No test file references these strings.
Step 5: Therefore the `*DB` method stubs have 0% test coverage. A re-implementation that restores DuckDB execution would pass existing CI.
findings.suggestion:
Add `pkg/expr/sql/db_test.go`:

```go
package sql

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/grafana/grafana-plugin-sdk-go/data"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestDBTablesListNotImplemented(t *testing.T) {
	db := NewInMemoryDB()
	_, err := db.TablesList("select * from foo")
	require.Error(t, err)
	require.Contains(t, err.Error(), "not implemented")
}

func TestDBRunCommandsNotImplemented(t *testing.T) {
	db := NewInMemoryDB()
	_, err := db.RunCommands([]string{"SELECT 1"})
	require.Error(t, err)
	require.Contains(t, err.Error(), "not implemented")
}

func TestDBQueryFramesIntoNotImplemented(t *testing.T) {
	db := NewInMemoryDB()
	err := db.QueryFramesInto("t", "SELECT 1", []*data.Frame{}, &data.Frame{})
	require.Error(t, err)
	require.Contains(t, err.Error(), "not implemented")
}
```

These tests are trivial but they lock in the stub contract and fail loudly if the stubs are replaced with real SQL execution without an explicit test update.
findings.title: db.go 'not implemented' stub methods have no tests — regression to a live SQL engine would not be caught

findings.blocking_reason: Skipped tests asserting outdated behavior are misleading but do not break the build or cause production impact.
findings.body:
Every test in `parser_test.go` (16 functions, lines 9-216) begins with `t.Skip()`, making the file a no-op in CI. Beyond being skipped, the tests assert the **old** behavior: they call `TablesList(sql)` (the package-level function in `parser.go:22`) and `assert.Nil(t, err)` — expecting success. But `TablesList` now calls `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands()`, which returns `errors.New("not implemented")`, so `TablesList` will always return an error wrapping `"error serializing sql: not implemented"`. If the `t.Skip()` calls were removed, **every test would fail** (they'd get a non-nil error where they assert nil, and `tables[0]` would panic on an empty slice).

This file is effectively dead code that misrepresents the current contract. It creates a false signal that the SQL parsing path is tested, when in reality it is neither tested nor functional. A reviewer reading `parser_test.go` without noticing the `t.Skip()` could believe the SQL Expressions feature has coverage.

**Recommendation:** Rather than leaving 16 skipped tests that assert the wrong behavior, either:
- Delete the file (the functionality is intentionally removed), or
- Replace it with a single test asserting that `TablesList` now returns an error (documenting the disabled posture), e.g. `_, err := TablesList("select * from foo"); require.Error(t, err); require.Contains(t, err.Error(), "not implemented")`.

This is a `suggestion` because the skipped tests cause no runtime failure — but they are actively misleading documentation and should not remain as-is in a security-critical package.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `parser_test.go` — each of the 16 test functions (`TestParse`, `TestParseWithComma`, `TestParseWithCommas`, `TestArray`, `TestArray2`, `TestXxx`, `TestParseSubquery`, `TestJoin`, `TestRightJoin`, `TestAliasWithJoin`, `TestAlias`, `TestError`, `TestParens`, `TestWith`, `TestWithQuote`, `TestWithQuote2`) starts with `t.Skip()`.
Step 2: Each test calls `TablesList(sql)` and `assert.Nil(t, err)` — expecting success.
Step 3: `parser.go:22-40` defines `TablesList`, which at line 26 calls `duckDB.RunCommands([]string{cmd})`. `db.go:16-18` defines `RunCommands` returning `"", errors.New("not implemented")`. Therefore `TablesList` always returns a non-nil error (wrapped as `"error serializing sql: not implemented"` at `parser.go:29`).
Step 4: If any `t.Skip()` were removed, the test would hit `assert.Nil(t, err)` with a non-nil error → failure, then potentially `tables[0]` on a nil/empty slice → panic.
Step 5: The file is dead, misleading, and asserts a contract that is the opposite of the current security posture.
findings.title: parser_test.go: all 16 tests are skipped and assert obsolete success behavior — rewrite to assert the 'not implemented' failure

findings.blocking_reason: The finding itself confirms SQL commands fail at the db.go stub returning 'not implemented', so there is no reachable exploit path; this is a defense-in-depth inconsistency, not a current vulnerability or regression.
findings.body:
`buildCMDNode` (nodes.go:109) has TWO code paths for parsing commands, and they apply the SQL gate inconsistently:

1. **FlagExpressionParser-ENABLED path** (lines 123-145): calls `reader.ReadQuery`, which hits reader.go:128-132 — this path IS gated by `enableSqlExpressions(h)` and rejects SQL with `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"`.

2. **FlagExpressionParser-DISABLED path** (lines 148-163, the `switch commandType`): `case TypeSQL:` (line 159-160) calls `UnmarshalSQLCommand(rn)` **directly, with NO `enableSqlExpressions` check**. `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (sql_command.go:51) calls `NewSQLCommand` (sql_command.go:25) which calls `sql.TablesList(rawSQL)` (sql_command.go:30).

This means the `enableSqlExpressions` gate in reader.go only protects ONE of the TWO code paths into `NewSQLCommand`. When `FlagExpressionParser` is not enabled globally, SQL commands flow through the switch statement unguarded.

**Current safety**: The vulnerability is still mitigated because `sql.TablesList` → `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands()` → `db.go` stub returns `errors.New("not implemented")` (db.go:17). So `NewSQLCommand` fails with `"error serializing sql: not implemented"`. Similarly `Execute` would fail at `QueryFramesInto` stub (db.go:21). The actual DuckDB engine is gone.

**Why this matters**: The PR's stated defense-in-depth model is "reader gate blocks SQL queries at the reader layer." But the gate is incomplete — it only covers the `FlagExpressionParser`-enabled branch. This is a mixed-state inconsistency: two entry points to the same SQL command, one gated, one not. If a future developer re-implements the `db.go` stubs (e.g., reintroduces a SQL engine), the nodes.go switch path would allow SQL commands to bypass the reader.go gate entirely whenever `FlagExpressionParser` is off (which is the default in many installations).

The error message also differs between paths: reader.go returns `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"` (line 131), while nodes.go path returns `"error serializing sql: not implemented"` (propagated from db.go stub). Inconsistent user-facing error behavior for the same disabled feature.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: nodes.go:123 `if toggles.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagExpressionParser)` — the gated path uses reader.ReadQuery (line 137) which checks enableSqlExpressions (reader.go:129).
Step 2: nodes.go:148 `switch commandType` — the fallback path (when FlagExpressionParser is OFF) reaches `case TypeSQL:` at line 159.
Step 3: nodes.go:160 `node.Command, err = UnmarshalSQLCommand(rn)` — NO call to enableSqlExpressions.
Step 4: sql_command.go:68 `UnmarshalSQLCommand` calls `NewSQLCommand(rn.RefID, expression)`.
Step 5: sql_command.go:30 `NewSQLCommand` calls `sql.TablesList(rawSQL)` → parser.go:23 `NewInMemoryDB()` → db.go:16-18 `RunCommands` returns `errors.New("not implemented")`.
Step 6: SQL command fails at DB stub, but the reader.go gate was bypassed. Two paths, one gated, one not — inconsistent defense-in-depth.
findings.suggestion: Add the same `enableSqlExpressions` gate to the `case TypeSQL:` branch in `buildCMDNode` (nodes.go:159-160), or — better — remove the `TypeSQL` case from the switch entirely and route all SQL parsing through the reader path. The cleanest fix is to delete the `case TypeSQL: node.Command, err = UnmarshalSQLCommand(rn)` lines and return an error for SQL command type in the switch, matching the reader.go gate behavior. This ensures there is exactly ONE place that decides whether SQL expressions are enabled, and both paths agree.
findings.title: buildCMDNode TypeSQL case bypasses enableSqlExpressions gate — inconsistent defense-in-depth

findings.blocking_reason: Dead code and cleanup suggestions do not break the build, tests, or any production behavior.
findings.body:
`parser.go` contains `TablesList` (line 22) plus three helper functions: `tablesFromAST` (line 43), `astError` (line 73), and `existsInList` (line 82). **The three helpers are completely unreachable.**

Control flow trace: `TablesList` (line 22) calls `NewInMemoryDB()` (db.go stub) then `duckDB.RunCommands([]string{cmd})` (line 26). `db.RunCommands` (db.go:16-18) unconditionally returns `errors.New("not implemented")`. Therefore `TablesList` ALWAYS returns an error at line 29 (`"error serializing sql: not implemented"`) and NEVER reaches line 39 `return tablesFromAST(ast)`. 

Consequently:
- `tablesFromAST` (lines 43-71): never called.
- `astError` (lines 73-80): only called from `tablesFromAST`, never called.
- `existsInList` (lines 82-89): only called from `tablesFromAST`, never called.
- Import `github.com/jeremywohl/flatten` (line 10): only used by `tablesFromAST`, dead.
- Import `encoding/json` (line 4): only used by `TablesList` line 33 `json.Unmarshal` — but that line is unreachable because `RunCommands` always errors first. Effectively dead.
- Import `sort` (line 6): only used by `tablesFromAST` line 66, dead.

The `strings` import (line 7) is still live (used at line 24 `strings.Replace` in `TablesList`). `fmt` (line 5) is still live (line 25, 29). `log` (line 9) is still live (line 28).

**Note on reachability of `TablesList` itself**: `TablesList` IS reachable via `NewSQLCommand` (sql_command.go:30) → `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (sql_command.go:68) → `buildCMDNode` TypeSQL case (nodes.go:160) when `FlagExpressionParser` is disabled. So `TablesList`'s lines 22-30 are reachable (but always error). Only lines 32-40 and the three helper functions are unreachable.

This is a mixed-state inconsistency: the file *looks* like a working SQL parser (89 lines, 4 imports, AST flattening, error handling, table deduplication) but is in fact a shell that always fails at the first DB call. A maintainer scanning the file will waste time understanding `tablesFromAST`/`astError`/`existsInList` logic that can never execute.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: parser.go:26 `ret, err := duckDB.RunCommands([]string{cmd})` — calls db.go:16 `func (db *DB) RunCommands(commands []string) (string, error) { return "", errors.New("not implemented") }`.
Step 2: db.go:17-18 unconditionally returns `"", errors.New("not implemented")`.
Step 3: parser.go:27 `if err != nil` is always true → parser.go:29 returns `nil, fmt.Errorf("error serializing sql: %s", err.Error())`.
Step 4: parser.go:39 `return tablesFromAST(ast)` is NEVER reached. `tablesFromAST` (line 43), `astError` (line 73), `existsInList` (line 82) are unreachable.
Step 5: Verified via grep — `tablesFromAST`, `astError`, `existsInList` have no callers outside parser.go. The only caller of `TablesList` is sql_command.go:30 (NewSQLCommand), which itself is only reachable via the ungated nodes.go:160 path.
findings.suggestion:
Two options:

1. **Delete the dead surface**: Remove `tablesFromAST`, `astError`, `existsInList`, and the unused imports (`encoding/json`, `sort`, `github.com/jeremywohl/flatten`). Reduce `TablesList` to a stub that returns an error directly, matching db.go's stub style: `func TablesList(rawSQL string) ([]string, error) { return nil, errors.New("not implemented") }`. This collapses parser.go from 89 lines to ~10.

2. **Mark the package deprecated**: Add a package-level comment `// Deprecated: SQL Expressions were removed in response to CVE-2024-9264. This package is retained only for compilation of sql_command.go and will be removed in a future release.` and consider moving the stub into sql_command.go itself.

Option 1 is preferred — it eliminates the dead code that prompted this review dimension. The `flatten` dependency (jeremywohl/flatten) can also be removed from go.mod if nothing else uses it.
findings.title: parser.go: 47 lines of unreachable helper functions (tablesFromAST, astError, existsInList) and 3 imports are dead code

findings.blocking_reason: Missing/skipped tests and low coverage are explicitly non-blocking per the bar; this is a test-coverage suggestion with no demonstrated production impact.
findings.body:
Every test in `pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go` (16 tests: TestParse, TestParseWithComma, ..., TestWithQuote2) begins with `t.Skip()`. The single test in `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go` (TestNewCommand) also begins with `t.Skip()`.

This means there is **zero test coverage** for:
1. `enableSqlExpressions` returning `false` (no assertion that the gate blocks SQL).
2. `reader.go` `QueryTypeSQL` case returning `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"`.
3. `NewSQLCommand` failing with `"error serializing sql: not implemented"` (the db.go stub error).
4. `SQLCommand.Execute` failing with `"not implemented"`.
5. The `nodes.go` `case TypeSQL:` path (ungated) producing the same/similar error.

This is a mixed-state inconsistency: the test files *exist* (suggesting coverage) but are entirely skipped (providing no coverage). A regression that re-enables SQL expressions (e.g., someone "fixes" `enableSqlExpressions` to return true, or re-implements the db.go stubs) would not be caught by any test.

The PR narrative explicitly calls out this gap: *"No Tests for the Gate"* is listed as a separate review dimension. This finding confirms that gap from the dead-code perspective: the skipped tests are themselves dead test code.
findings.evidence: Step 1: parser_test.go:10 `t.Skip()` in TestParse. Step 2: parser_test.go:19 `t.Skip()` in TestParseWithComma. ... Step 3: parser_test.go:201 `t.Skip()` in TestWithQuote2. All 16 tests skip. Step 4: sql_command_test.go:9 `t.Skip()` in TestNewCommand. Step 5: `go test ./pkg/expr/sql/...` would report 0 run, 16 skipped — no assertions execute. No test verifies enableSqlExpressions, the reader.go error, or the stub errors.
findings.title: All 16 parser tests and the sql_command test are t.Skip()'d — no test verifies the gate or the always-fail behavior

findings.blocking_reason: Dead code after an intentional stub error return is a code-quality/maintainability concern, not a build, security, data-loss, API-contract, or behavioral regression issue.
findings.body:
`SQLCommand.Execute` (sql_command.go:79-121) is the runtime execution path for SQL commands. Even if a `SQLCommand` is successfully constructed (via the ungated `nodes.go` switch path described in the nodes.go finding), `Execute` will always fail:

- Line 96: `db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()` returns the stub `DB{}`.
- Line 100: `err := db.QueryFramesInto(gr.refID, gr.query, allFrames, frame)` calls db.go:20-22 which returns `errors.New("not implemented")`.
- Line 101-104: `err != nil` → sets `rsp.Error = err` and returns.

So lines 106-120 (frame RefID assignment, no-data handling, `TableData` wrapping) are **unreachable** — `QueryFramesInto` always errors before reaching them. The entire method body after the stub call is dead.

This is a mixed-state inconsistency: the `Execute` method *appears* to implement SQL query execution (frame assembly, refID assignment, no-data handling, TableData wrapping) but is a facade that always returns an error from the stub. A maintainer reading this will believe Grafana can execute SQL expressions when it cannot.

Note: `NeedsVars` (line 73) and `Type` (line 123) are trivially live (return struct fields/constants), so the `SQLCommand` type itself is not entirely dead — it satisfies the `Command` interface for compilation. But the runtime behavior is always-fail.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: sql_command.go:96 `db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()` → db.go:24-26 returns `&DB{}`.
Step 2: sql_command.go:100 `err := db.QueryFramesInto(gr.refID, gr.query, allFrames, frame)` → db.go:20-22 `func (db *DB) QueryFramesInto(...) error { return errors.New("not implemented") }`.
Step 3: sql_command.go:101 `if err != nil` always true → line 103 `rsp.Error = err`, line 104 `return rsp, nil`.
Step 4: Lines 106-120 (`frame.RefID = gr.refID`, no-data `mathexp.NoData`, `mathexp.TableData` wrapping) are never reached. Effectively dead code.
findings.title: SQLCommand.Execute body is effectively dead — always fails at QueryFramesInto stub

findings.blocking_reason: Documentation and flag exposure contradicting behavior is a code quality/consistency issue, not a build break, security vulnerability, data loss, API contract break, or behavioral regression.
findings.body: The flag is still registered in registry.go:1083, exposed in frontend types.ts:73 and featureToggles.gen.ts:164, and documented as "Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions as Expressions" — all of which is now false. The PR author acknowledged this and deferred it; this finding ensures it's not forgotten.
findings.suggestion: Remove the flag entirely — delete from toggles_gen.go, registry.go, toggles_gen.json, frontend types. Replace call site with unconditional error return.
findings.title: Flag doc and user-facing exposure contradict behavior

findings.blocking_reason: Skipped tests asserting stale behavior do not break the build, tests, or any production code path.
findings.body: All 16 test functions in `parser_test.go` are guarded by `t.Skip()` so they don't cause CI failures, but they assert against the **removed DuckDB parsing behavior** — expecting `TablesList` to return `nil` error and specific table lists. After the PR, `DB.RunCommands` always returns `errors.New("not implemented")`, which propagates through the package-level `TablesList` in `parser.go`. If anyone un-skips these tests, 15 of 16 would immediately fail. The PR should have deleted or updated these tests to match the stubbed reality.

findings.blocking_reason: Stale go.work.sum hash entries are non-blocking clutter; the Go toolchain ignores them and the finding confirms the build is not broken.
findings.body:
The PR removes `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck` and several indirect dependencies from `go.mod` and `go.sum`, but `go.work.sum` still contains hash entries for them:

- `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck v0.3.1` (lines 891-892)
- `github.com/JohnCGriffin/overflow v0.0.0-20211019200055-46fa312c352c` (line 312)
- `github.com/apache/thrift v0.20.0` (lines 371-372)
- `github.com/klauspost/asmfmt v1.3.2` (line 707)
- `github.com/minio/asm2plan9s v0.0.0-20200509001527-cdd76441f9d8` (line 755)
- `github.com/minio/c2goasm v0.0.0-20190812172519-36a3d3bbc4f3` (line 756)

This is **not build-breaking** — `go.work.sum` is an auto-managed workspace hash file and the Go toolchain ignores entries for modules that are no longer in the dependency graph. However, it leaves stale clutter that could confuse future audits or `go work sync` operations. Running `go work sync` (or `go mod tidy` in workspace mode) would prune these entries.

**Core build-breakage verification (PASS):** A repository-wide `rg` search for all 10 removed modules across all `.go` files (including tests) returned **zero matches**. No remaining code imports any removed module. `github.com/jeremywohl/flatten v1.0.1` is correctly retained as a direct dependency in `go.mod` (line 327) and is actively used at `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:44` (`flatten.Flatten(ast[0], "", flatten.DotStyle)`). `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` no longer imports `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck`. `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` is a 26-line stub with no go-duck import. The dependency removal is mechanically safe — `go build ./...` will not fail from missing imports.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: Ran `rg -n 'github.com/scottlepp/go-duck|github.com/JohnCGriffin/overflow|github.com/apache/thrift|github.com/klauspost/asmfmt|github.com/minio/asm2plan9s|github.com/minio/c2goasm|github.com/hairyhenderson/go-which|github.com/iancoleman/orderedmap|github.com/araddon/dateparse|github.com/google/go-replayers' --type go` → no output (zero matches across entire repo).
Step 2: Ran `rg -n 'jeremywohl/flatten' go.mod` → line 327: `github.com/jeremywohl/flatten v1.0.1 // @grafana/grafana-app-platform-squad` (direct dep, not indirect).
Step 3: Ran `rg -n 'scottlepp/go-duck' go.work.sum` → lines 891-892 still present (stale workspace hashes).
Step 4: Verified `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` imports only `encoding/json`, `fmt`, `sort`, `strings`, `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/infra/log`, `github.com/jeremywohl/flatten` — no go-duck.
Step 5: Verified `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` is 26-line stub returning `errors.New("not implemented")` with no go-duck import.
findings.suggestion: Run `go work sync` to prune stale entries from go.work.sum, or manually remove the six listed module hash lines. This is cosmetic and non-blocking.
findings.title: go.work.sum retains stale hashes for removed modules (go-duck, overflow, thrift, asmfmt, asm2plan9s, c2goasm)
